question: Which transaction states and recovery transitions preserve the appearance of atomic commit under a bounded rollback and reopen protocol?

carrier.description: Finite states observed or modeled by the bounded sequential protocol.

state_space.description: A single connection seeds committed rows, encounters a duplicate-key failure, explicitly rolls back, commits a new transaction, and is reopened for inspection.

transitions.name: Seed then duplicate-key failure
transitions.label: insert fifth row then duplicate primary key

transitions.name: Subsequent commit
transitions.label: commit fifth row in a new transaction

laws_or_checks.name: Initial state
laws_or_checks.description: The protocol begins in the seeded state.

laws_or_checks.name: Transition closure
laws_or_checks.description: Declared transitions remain within the finite state carrier.

assumptions: The model covers one fixed sequential protocol and does not model process crashes or power loss.
The explicit application rollback is distinguished from automatic crash recovery.
The model abstracts SQLite pager, journal, filesystem, and concurrency internals.

conditions: SQLite default journal and synchronous settings

classification.reason: All transitions are closed over the declared state space.

conditions: SQLite default journal and synchronous settings

result.summary: Under the fixed sequential protocol, explicit rollback restored the committed seed state and a subsequent transaction remained readable after close and reopen.

limitations: This observes application-requested rollback, not process crash or power-loss recovery.
The fixed five-row dataset and three repetitions do not establish a general atomicity or durability theorem.

result.summary: The G5 protocol did not test process crash, power loss, or automatic recovery after interruption.

validation_records.question: Did the G5 protocol establish crash or power-loss recovery behavior?
validation_records.what_not_established: No crash-recovery, power-loss, or automatic-interruption recovery result was established.
limitations: This is an absence-of-evidence record, not a negative finding about SQLite.
A dedicated fault-injection protocol is required for those conditions.
